hints: Focus on what 'had not changed in size' really tells you: there was no net gain or loss of water by osmosis after 30 minutes.
Remember water moves in response to water potential, not just sucrose concentration, and potato cells contain many different solutes plus pressure effects.
walkthrough:
**Observe what no change means**

Think like a detective. If the potato piece is the same size, it has not gained water (would swell) and has not lost water (would shrink).

That means there is no net movement of water by osmosis.

**Apply the water potential rule**

Osmosis always gives a net flow from higher water potential to lower water potential.

No net flow means the two sides must be balanced:
$$\text{water potential of potato} = \text{water potential of solution}$$

**Check each statement carefully**

Statement 2 is exactly what we just deduced, so it is true.

Statement 1 is tempting but wrong. Potato sap contains glucose, amino acids, ions and many other solutes, not just sucrose. Equal water potential does not mean equal sucrose concentration.

Statement 3 is also wrong. Water molecules keep crossing the membrane both ways all the time. We just have equal movement in and out, so net movement is zero.

options.A: Includes 1 and 3 which are both false. Equal water potential does not mean equal sucrose, and water still moves both ways with no net change.
options.B: Includes 1 which is false. The potato has many solutes besides sucrose, so matching water potential does not prove matching sucrose concentration.
options.C: Includes 1 and 3 which are both false. Only statement 2 can be safely concluded.
options.D: Correct, only 2 is true. No change in size shows no net osmosis, so water potential inside and outside must be equal.
